summary.en: Academies form competence; Expert Teams deliver Services; Macro Works contain them; Meta Solutions coordinate across them; Projects instantiate the whole.

description.en: The six feature labels are not a flat list. They form a stacked ontology in which each layer answers a different question and each layer constrains the one below it.

lead.en: Projects instantiate Meta Solutions; Meta Solutions operate on Macro Works; Macro Works contain Services; Services are delivered by Expert Teams; Academies form the competence that Expert Teams require.

title.en: The full stack in one view

lead.en: Each layer answers a different question and constrains the one below it. Read top-down: what is built, what coordinates it, what contains it, what is commissioned, who delivers it, who is competent to deliver.

question.en: What is being built, for whom, by when?

body.en: A time-bound instantiation. A project may consume several services, invoke several meta-solutions, and produce a concrete artefact or programme. It is not the same kind of entity as a service.

Reusable instruments any service can invoke: identity, credentialing, workflow, evidence, sampling, audit, publication. Deliberately NOT a sixth macro — the meta layer sits above the macro partition so it never becomes a domain.
The top-level partition of the demand space. Each macro answers a distinct domain question — meaning, shelter, knowledge, rules, deployable technique — and carries a distinct Real/Virtual placement.

The atomic, contractible unit of work. Each service carries a canonical ID, a macro placement, a proposed Dyon profile, an expert degree-field cluster, a weekly deliverable set with evidence rules, and declared cross-macro edges.
The service-level delivery unit: one manager plus about ten experts, producing accepted outputs against a service-specific rubric. Not a cross-service entity.
MetaX Academy and the Dyon certification profiles. Academies produce the assessed competence that expert teams consume: entry competence before assignment, continuing competence throughout.

feedback.en: Feedback flows upward — a service team's acceptance data can inform academy curriculum; a project's delivery experience can revise a meta-solution; a macro's cross-dependency friction can revise the ontology. The constitutive relationships — what makes what possible — flow downward.

note.en: Without academies, no assessed teams; without teams, no delivered services; without services, no macro substance; without meta-solutions, no coherent cross-service coordination; without projects, no concrete instantiation.
Every figure is a variable in config/variables.php; none is typed into a page.

title.en: The dependency direction at each step

lead.en: The arrows are not all one-directional in practice, but the constitutive ones are.

value.en: Academies → Expert Teams. Academies produce the assessed competence; teams consume it.
Services → Expert Teams (constitutive). The service is the work definition; the team is the accountable producer.
Macro Works → Services. No service exists outside a macro; no macro is merely a label without services.
Meta Solutions → Services (as instruments), not Services → Meta Solutions.
Projects → Meta Solutions + Services. Projects are downstream of both.

lead.en: A project is not the same kind of entity as a service. A service is a repeatable unit of commissioned work; a project is a time-bound instantiation that may consume several services, invoke several meta-solutions and produce a concrete artefact or programme.

body.en: A project is the only layer that answers "what is being built, for whom, by when?". Everything else is what makes that answer possible.

title.en: Drop one layer and state what breaks

body.en: Remove a layer and the layer below loses its precondition. That test is how the ontology is checked, not how it is asserted.

title.en: Keep the meta layer above the partition

body.en: Meta Solutions are instruments. If they became a sixth macro, the five-macro partition would stop being a partition.
The load-bearing gaps below are what make this relationship credible rather than aspirational.
These are not footnotes. They are the conditions under which the stack is credible.
